audit.whatIsWrong: Three places call Riptide his ultimate: spikes[1] 'His Riptide ultimate knocks you airborne and chains into his hook', content.mid 'At level 6 Nautilus's Riptide adds an airborne', whys[4] 'His Riptide ultimate shifts the balance'.
audit.why: Riptide is his E — three exploding waves that damage and slow, 600 range, 7s at rank 1, available from level 2. His ultimate is Depth Charge: a tracking shockwave, 825 range, that knocks up everyone it passes and knocks up plus stuns its target, on 120/100/80s. A player watching for 'Riptide at 6' is watching the wrong ability and will misread both the level-6 threat and the 120-second window after he spends it.
audit.corrected: Depth Charge is the level-6 ability. Riptide is his E and has been up since level 2.
sources: champ-data/_kits/nautilus.json E Riptide, R Depth Charge

audit.whatIsWrong: content.early tells the player to 'stand at max Tongue Lash range' to be safe from the hook, and whys[1] says to 'respect the hook range' without giving it.
audit.why: Dredge Line is 1150. Tongue Lash is 900. Max Tongue Lash range is 250 units INSIDE hook range — the advice as written puts the player exactly where Nautilus wants him and calls it safe. This is the most consequential error in the entry.
audit.corrected: There is no poke range that is safe from the hook. Respect 1150, not 900 — if you are close enough to Tongue Lash him, he can hook you.

audit.whatIsWrong: The passive is described as a chaining, repeating root: 'his passive roots your ankles on every auto', 'chain his passive root into a full trade', 'his auto-passive roots limit your ability to stick', 'Eat his passive root chain'.
audit.why: Staggering Blow roots on his FIRST attack against a target, not on every attack. It is one root that opens a trade, not a chain that sustains one. Believing you are locked down for the whole exchange discourages the retrade that Tahm Kench actually wins.
audit.corrected: Staggering Blow roots on his first attack against you. After it, the lockdown is whatever he lands with Dredge Line and Depth Charge.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid and content.late route level 6 and objective play through 'Abyssal Voyage' — 'a roam and repositioning tool', 'Abyssal Voyage to carry your ADC through dragon fights'.
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage is the pre-rework ultimate and is not in the current kit. Level 6 gives Devour. The ally-carry fantasy the text describes does not exist; what does exist is that Devour shields an ally, and unlike devouring an enemy it needs no An Acquired Taste stacks.
audit.corrected: Devour shields an ally and needs no stacks to do it; eating Nautilus needs three.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[0] and content.mid teach 'chain the stun into Devour' / 'Q-stun him ... and Devour the follow-up'.
audit.why: Tongue Lash on a three-stack target stuns and consumes the stacks; devouring an enemy champion requires three stacks. One set pays for one of the two.
audit.corrected: Three stacks buys the Q-stun or the Devour, not both.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry is built entirely on tracking Dredge Line but never states its cooldown.
audit.why: 'Commit the moment it is down' is unusable without the length of the window.
audit.corrected: Dredge Line 14/13/12/11/10s at 1150 range. Depth Charge 120/100/80s at 825. Riptide 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s at 600. Titan's Wrath 12s flat.

audit.whatIsWrong: Titan's Wrath is never mentioned in the content layer despite being the reason short trades into him stall.
audit.why: It is a 12-second flat cooldown shield whose duration also makes his attacks deal area damage over time. Committing three stacks into a live Titan's Wrath spends the whole An Acquired Taste cycle against a shield.
audit.corrected: Do not spend the stack cycle into a live Titan's Wrath — it is 12s flat, so it is the shortest wait in his kit.

audit.why: 51.65% over 2060 games — the largest sample in this slice — and the chart reads Skill 3 / Nautilus 2 / Tahm Kench 2. An early Nautilus window resolving into a Tahm Kench item-scaling finish is exactly the right shape for a near-even number. No change.

The packet's five suspectNames for this matchup ('Stack An Acquired Taste', 'Acquired Taste', 'His Dredge Line', 'Thick Skin's', 'Dredge Line's') are all false positives — possessives and partial quotes of correct names. The real errors here were the ones the detector could not see: Riptide labelled as the ultimate, and the hook range.

edits.after: Depth Charge knocks you airborne and chains into his hook — but Devour can now swallow him out of his own engage, provided you already hold three stacks.

edits.before: At level 1 neither of you has a decisive edge — his passive roots your ankles on every auto and your Tongue Lash slow matches his control. Contest the wave with Q pokes but never stand in a position where a level-1 Dredge Line can drag you into his wave. The moment he gets level 2 and Dredge Line is live, the lane shifts to him: he can hook you mid-stack-building and chain his passive root into a full trade before you reach 3 stacks. Respect the hook completely at levels 2-3 — stand at max Tongue Lash range, let him waste it on minions or a bad angle, then immediately run your full pattern into him once it is down.
edits.after: At level 1 neither of you has a decisive edge — Staggering Blow roots on his first attack against you, not on every one, and your Tongue Lash slow matches that control. Contest the wave with Q pokes, but understand the geometry first: Dredge Line reaches 1150 and Tongue Lash only 900, so there is no poke range that sits outside his hook. Max Tongue Lash range is 250 units inside it. Respect 1150 at levels 2-3 — bait the hook onto minions or a bad angle, count the 14 seconds at rank 1, and run your full pattern into him while it is down. Do not spend the stack cycle into a live Titan's Wrath; that shield is only 12 seconds, so it is the cheapest thing in his kit to wait out.

edits.before: His Dredge Line is the matchup's fulcrum — when it is up you play passive and fish for stacks at range; when it is down you commit. At level 6 Nautilus's Riptide adds an airborne that resets the root chain, so always have Thick Skin's active queued before his ultimate animation completes — convert the grey health into a shield and deny him the burst window. With Dredge Line down, walk up, land Tongue Lash to 3 stacks, chain the stun into Devour, and out-sustain the retrade with grey-health healing. Abyssal Voyage is a roam and repositioning tool here — not a trading button — use it to cover bot when Nautilus TPing to dragon is his only way back into the game.
edits.after: His Dredge Line is the matchup's fulcrum — when it is up you fish for stacks at range; when it is down, all 14 seconds of it, you commit. At level 6 it is Depth Charge, not Riptide, that adds the airborne — Riptide is his E and has been up since level 2, which is why the slow never seems to end — so have Thick Skin's active queued before his ultimate lands and convert the grey health into a shield. With Dredge Line down, walk up, stack to three, then choose: Tongue Lash to stun him off the wave, or Devour to remove him outright. Abyssal Dive is your reposition and it is 21 seconds; its knockup makes it an engage, not a trading button.

edits.before: Heartsteel and a second tank item make you effectively unkillable in isolated 1v1 range — your grey-health pool regenerates faster than Nautilus's auto damage depletes it, and Devour lets you remove him from any fight at the critical moment. The lane is already yours, so shift your focus to objective setup: Abyssal Voyage to carry your ADC through dragon fights, Devour peeling his Dredge Line target, and forcing Nautilus to burn his hook on you in the frontline instead of his real targets. At 2-plus items he is not a scaling threat that outgrows you — he is a crowd-control bot you have already learned to eat.
edits.after: Heartsteel and a second tank item make you effectively unkillable in isolated 1v1 range — your grey-health pool regenerates faster than Nautilus's auto damage depletes it, and Devour lets you remove him from any fight at the critical moment. The lane is already yours, so shift to objective setup: Devour shields an ally and costs no stacks to do it, so the peel on his Dredge Line target is always available even when the eat is not. Force him to burn the hook on you in the frontline. At 2-plus items he is a crowd-control bot you have already learned to eat.

notes: The packet's suspectNames detector produced five false positives for this matchup and missed the two errors that actually matter: Riptide is labelled as Nautilus's ultimate in three places (it is his E, up from level 2; the ultimate is Depth Charge), and content.early instructs the player to stand at max Tongue Lash range for safety when Dredge Line outranges Tongue Lash 1150 to 900. The second one is actively dangerous advice — it tells the player the exact spot Nautilus wants him in and calls it safe. Worth checking whether the same 'stand at max Q range' boilerplate is applied to other long-range engage champions across this file. The champion-wide 'Abyssal Voyage' problem reported in tahmkench__mel.json affects both content.mid and content.late here, and content.late in particular describes an ally-carry ultimate that no longer exists. No WKM_LINES errors observed for this matchup.
